requirement_source: User: interactive asset with mouse-to-gamepad output and real-gamepad-to-asset motion

canonical_adapter.reason: The schema-1 viewer rig is not generated from, or structurally validated against, the canonical schema-2 body/joint graph. It cannot prove preservation of coupled constraints, virtual frames, contact data or inverse mappings.

delivery.primary_platform: Browser-local 3D inspection viewer served on localhost; actual meshes stored on GPU node and reachable through an explicit asset route
delivery.rationale: Browser Gamepad API can read the controller attached to the user's own computer; GPU node does not need USB forwarding
delivery.blender: Keep exported part names and assembly transforms portable; Blender alone is not the chosen live Gamepad API frontend
delivery.network: Localhost or HTTPS for browser device access; no public server binding or automatic hardware actuation
not_accepted_as_substitute: state sliders without manipulating mesh parts

mouse.input: Pick and manipulate actual visible stick, trigger, button and D-pad meshes
mouse.path: pointer -> constrained part pose -> schema-1 preview mapping -> gamepad state; this path is not the canonical schema-2 physical mapping until the adapter gate passes
mouse.display: Part identity, joint coordinates, axes, analog triggers, button values, sample timestamp and parameter provenance
mouse.release: Explicit return/hold UI policy, labeled as kinematic preview until restoring dynamics are validated

device.input: Real controller on user's computer through navigator.getGamepads()
device.path: device -> standard gamepad state -> schema-1 preview mapping -> actual mesh part motion; this does not establish canonical schema-2 roundtrip equivalence
device.display: Device ID, standard mapping status, raw state, represented state, missing controls, receipt time and source timestamp
device.arbitration: Mouse cannot overwrite device-mode values; changing mode, device disconnect, focus loss and pointer cancel must not leave stale commands

shared_mapping.layout: 4 standard axes followed by 17 standard button values; 21 floats is our serialization choice, W3C specifies separate arrays
shared_mapping.unknown_mapping: Reject unrecognized device layouts, do not guess axis order
shared_mapping.differentiability: Keep analog values as floats, no binarization in signal transport. JS device capture is not autograd; later Torch pose/state mapping needs its own gradient tests.
shared_mapping.canonical_mapping_status: blocked until a fail-closed, schema-validated schema-2-to-viewer adapter is implemented and verified
shared_mapping.estimate_policy: User permits estimated physical parameters before measurement. A parameter may be estimated from cited geometry or component evidence with derivation and uncertainty. This does not require prior physical calibration. Unsupported and uninferable parameters remain null; synthetic software fixtures do not supply target parameter values.

acceptance_gates.check: Fail closed unless a schema-validated adapter preserves the canonical body/joint graph, joint curves, coupled domains, virtual-frame semantics and inverse input mappings; unsupported constructs must be rejected, not dropped.
The owner selected Xbox One S and approved the downloaded BatonyRobson asset as the target appearance. Metric geometry and mechanics have separate acceptance fields.
Visible mesh manipulation produces the correct signed axes and corresponding button/trigger signals
User's real Xbox One S drives all available controls, including simultaneous independent controls
state->pose->state tested on neutral, endpoints, diagonals and concurrent inputs; losses/restrictions reported
No stuck inputs after disconnect, focus loss, pointer cancellation or mode switch
Record mouse and physical-controller demonstration; inspect wrong axes, pivots, detachment and interpenetration

physics_separation: Both interactive paths are required for v1 acceptance. Their success alone does not validate forces, friction, damping or finger contact; those remain separately labeled.
